title: Rust: Even or Odd
description: Check if a number is even or odd using the modulo operator.

steps.title: Check if Even
steps.description: Write a function `is_even(n: i32) -> bool` that returns true if n is even. Call with 4 and 7, print both results.
hints: The modulo operator `%` returns the remainder.

verification.failureMessage: Check if 4 is even (true) and 7 is even (false).

steps.title: Print Even or Odd
steps.description: Write a program that checks if `n = 15` is even or odd and prints `"Even"` or `"Odd"`.

verification.failureMessage: Print whether 15 is Even or Odd.

steps.title: Check Multiple Numbers
steps.description: Write a loop that checks numbers 1 through 10 and prints whether each is even or odd.
hints: Print like `println!("{} is {}", i, if i%2==0{"even"}else{"odd"});`

verification.test: output.includes('1 is odd') || output.includes('2 is even')
verification.failureMessage: Print whether each number 1-10 is even or odd.

steps.title: Count Evens and Odds
steps.description: From `[4, 7, 2, 9, 10, 15, 22]`, count how many are even and how many are odd. Print both counts.
hints: Loop through the array, increment the appropriate counter.

verification.failureMessage: Print the count of evens (4) and odds (3).

steps.title: Ternary-Style Return
steps.description: Write a function `even_or_odd(n: i32) -> &'static str` that returns `"even"` or `"odd"`. Call with 42 and print the result.
hints: `if n % 2 == 0 { "even" } else { "odd" }` this is an expression!
The return type is `&'static str` (string literal).
